source_text: Διὰ τί γάρ, ἄνδρες Ἕλληνες, ὥσπερ ἐν πυγμῇ συγκρούειν βούλεσθε τὰς πολιτείας καθ᾿ ἡμῶν; Καὶ εἰ μὴ τοῖς τινῶν νομίμοις συγχρῆσθαι βούλομαι, τίνος χάριν καθάπερ μιαρώτατος μεμίσημαι; Προστάττει φόρους τελεῖν ὁ βασιλεύς; Ἕτοιμος παρέχειν. Δουλεύειν ὁ δεσπότης καὶ ὑπηρετεῖν; Τὴν δουλείαν γινώσκων. Τὸν μὲν γὰρ ἄνθρωπον ἀνθρωπίνως τιμητέον, φοβητέον δὲ μόνον τὸν θεόν· ὅστις ἀνθρωπίνοις οὐκ ἔστιν ὁρατὸς ὀφθαλμοῖς, οὐ τέχνῃ περιληπτός. Τοῦτον μόνον ἀρνεῖσθαι κελευόμενος οὐ πεισθήσομαι, τεθνήξομαι δὲ μᾶλλον, ἵνα μὴ ψεύστης καὶ ἀχάριστος ἀποδειχθῶ. Θεὸς ὁ καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς οὐκ ἔχει σύστασιν ἐν χρόνῳ, μόνος ἄναρχος ὢν καὶ αὐτὸς ὑπάρχων τῶν ὅλων ἀρχή. Πνεῦμα ὁ θεός, οὐ διήκων διὰ τῆς ὕλης, πνευμάτων δὲ ὑλικῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ σχημάτων κατασκευαστής· ἀόρατός τε καὶ ἀναφής, αἰσθητῶν καὶ ἀοράτων αὐτὸς γεγονὼς πατήρ.Τοῦτον διὰ τῆς ποιήσεως αὐτοῦ ἴσμεν, καὶ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀόρατον τοῖς ποιήμασι καταλαμβανόμεθα. Δημιουργίαν τὴν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ γεγενημένην χάριν ἡμῶν προσκυνεῖν οὐ θέλω. Γέγονεν ἥλιος καὶ σελήνη δι᾿ ἡμᾶς· εἶτα πῶς τοὺς ἐμοὺς ὑπηρέτας προσκυνήσω; Πῶς δὲ ξύλα καὶ λίθους θεοὺς ἀποφανοῦμαι; Πνεῦμα γὰρ τὸ διὰ τῆς ὕλης διῆκον ἔλαττον ὑπάρχει τοῦ θειοτέρου πνεύματος· ὅπερ δὲ ψυχῇ παρωμοιωμένον οὐ τιμητέον ἐπ᾿ ἴσης τῷ τελείῳ θεῷ. Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ τὸν ἀνωνόμαστον θεὸν δωροδοκητέον· ὁ γὰρ πάντων ἀνενδεὴς οὐ διαβλητέος ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν ὡς ἐνδεής. Φανερώτερον δὲ ἐκθήσομαι τὰ ἡμέτερα.
pass_a_gloss: For what reason, men Greeks, do you want to clash the cities against us as in a fistfight? And if I do not want to use the laws of some, for whose sake have I been hated as most defiled? Does the king command to pay taxes? I am ready to provide. Does the master command to serve and be a slave? I know the slavery. For the man is to be honored in a human way, but only God is to be feared; who is not visible to human eyes, not comprehended by skill. This one only, being commanded to deny, I will not be persuaded, but I will die rather, so that I may not be shown to be a liar and ungrateful. God, the one according to us, does not have a beginning in time, being alone without a beginning and himself being the beginning of all things. God is Spirit, not passing through matter, but the creator of material spirits and the forms in it; invisible and ungraspable, himself having become the Father of visible and invisible things. We know this one through his creation, and we grasp the invisible of his power through his works. I do not want to worship the creation that has come into being under him for our sake. The sun and moon have come into being for our sake; then how will I worship my servants? How will I declare wood and stones to be gods? For the Spirit that passes through matter is less than the more divine Spirit; and what is likened to the soul is not to be honored equally with the perfect God. But neither should the unnamed God be bribed; for he who is in need of nothing is not to be slandered by us as if he were in need. I will exhibit our things more clearly.

choices.why: refers to the creation of spirits

pass_b_english: Why, men of Greece, do you want to crash your cities against us like fistfighters? If I refuse to follow certain laws, why have I been hated as the most defiled? When the king commands taxes, I am ready to pay. When a master commands service and slavery, I accept that lot. For a human being deserves human honor, but God alone deserves fear. He cannot be seen by human eyes or grasped by human skill. Even if I am commanded to deny Him alone, I will not be persuaded; I would rather die than be exposed as a liar and ingrate. The God we worship has no beginning in time; He alone is unbegotten and is Himself the source of all things. God is Spirit. He does not pass through matter, but creates material spirits and the forms within it. Invisible and intangible, He has become the Father of all things visible and invisible. We know Him through His creation, and through His works we perceive His invisible power. I will not worship the creation that came into being under Him for our sake. The sun and moon were made for our benefit; why then would I worship my own servants? Why would I declare wood and stones to be gods? The spirit that passes through matter is inferior to the more divine Spirit, and what merely resembles the soul must not be honored on the same level as the perfect God. Nor should the unnamed God be bribed, for He who lacks nothing must not be slandered by us as if He were needy. I will set out our beliefs more clearly.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the theological nuances of the Greek text, particularly the distinctions regarding God's nature (Spirit, unbegotten/without beginning) and the relationship between the material and divine. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
